US healthcare costs are rising at an alarming rate:

Medical care prices have surged +132% since 2000, the largest increase among major consumer spending categories.

Over the same period, shelter costs have risen +127%, while food prices have soared +112%.

Price increases across all these spending categories have outpaced overall CPI, which is up +99% since 2000.

As a result, ~30% of insured US adults have skipped or delayed getting healthcare they needed due to costs over the last 12 months, according to a KFF survey.

Healthcare costs have never been higher.

BREAKING: US retirement assets surged +$3.8 trillion in Q2 2026, or +7.9%, to a record $51.2 trillion.

The increase was led by assets in individual retirement accounts (IRAs), which jumped +$1.7 trillion, or +9.2%, to $19.9 trillion, an all-time high.

Since 2022, total US retirement assets have soared +$16 trillion, or +45.5%.

Asset owners are seeing unprecedented gains.

The global copper market is extremely tight:

China's copper import premium over London Metal Exchange (LME) prices has surpassed $200 per ton, the largest premium on record.

The Yangshan premium, named after a Shanghai port that serves as a major hub for Chinese copper imports, has more than doubled over the last 3 months.

Since the beginning of 2026, this figure has surged +700%.

Furthermore, the premium of spot prices over three-month futures on the LME widened to $217 per ton, the largest since mid-August.

This has been driven by strong Chinese copper demand and domestic inventories falling below typical seasonal levels.

At the same time, expectations of potential US tariffs on refined copper have redirected hundreds of thousands of tons of copper to the US, leaving global inventories heavily concentrated in the country.

The physical copper supply squeeze is far from over.

In The Stolguard Incident and other fiction I'm writing, I tend to be in a transitional camp.

I explore deeply gray and disturbing areas, acknowledging major ethical complexity, but with themes that point toward virtue rather than nihilism.
https://t.co/Yqy5uoHWyX

Fiction goes through various pendulum swings, tied to the public zeitgeist.

Sometimes the dominant content is too simplistically black/white and there is a demand for more gritty/gray/realistic stuff.

And then the dominant content eventually gets too gritty and borderline nihilistic, and people are like “I want some stories about clear heroes, actually.”

Think Lord of the Rings (almost pure good vs evil) vs Game of Thrones (everyone’s gray, with varying shades).

Star Trek TNG was in that Lord of the Rings camp where virtue was broad among the protagonists and it was the details that people debated over.

Some people debate which type of fiction is “better”, but I think both are useful, and the pendulum, the zeitgeist, must be respected.

Both utopian and dystopian worlds are thematically useful to explore, and when they trend toward extremes of marketshare, it’s inevitable and useful that counter-voices emerge and push the other way.

BREAKING: South Korea’s economy grew +1.0% QoQ in Q3 2026, marking its 3rd consecutive quarterly expansion, beating expectations of +0.8%.

Exports were the main driver, rising +2.3% on stronger semiconductor, machinery and electrical equipment shipments.

Facility investment surged +4.1%, particularly reflecting increased spending on machinery, including semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

YoY, South Korea's economy grew +3.4%, exceeding expectations of +3.0% and following +3.7% and +3.8% growth in Q2 and Q3, respectively.

South Korea is now on track to surpass $1 trillion in annual exports for the first time in 2026, making it only the 4th economy after the US, China, and Germany to reach this threshold.

South Korea is seeing a historic economic transformation.

As a % of GDP, this metric is up to a record 5.4%, significantly surpassing the previous high of 4.5% recorded in Q4 2000.

The scale of US AI investment is unlike anything seen before.
